model_interpretation.claim: On mixed-width input, selecting widths and checking special lead-byte bounds through the baseline's scalar branch tree may cost more control flow than a compact state DFA. This pure-scalar candidate retains ASCII run skipping and uses byte classes plus DFA transitions to test whether fewer width-specific branches help; table lookup costs may offset any benefit.

model_interpretation.claim: The baseline and previous lead-directed candidate retain the same general scalar width dispatch, but the latter was slower. This pure-scalar variant tests whether aggregating per-sequence validity predicates with bitwise OR, rather than short-circuit OR, reduces control-flow or dependency overhead on mixed-width input. It keeps the ASCII scan and checks remaining length before every continuation-byte load. The compiler may produce equivalent code or the extra predicate work may outweigh any benefit; performance is unmeasured.

items.subject: Branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 decoding
items.objective: Primary hypothesis: reducing scalar decoding control flow or dependencies helps the mixed-width workload; the supplied baseline already has an ASCII fast path, so do not assume ASCII scanning is the only scalar cost. Compare the baseline decoder with compact-state/DFA or reduced-branch scalar variants, measuring each under the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and checking official ASCII/malformed correctness. Keep scalar decoding as the focus, but do not treat that focus as a ban on useful correctness-preserving experiments; label any hybrid separately from pure-scalar results. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, bounds, and thread budget. Report failed variants.
